title: CVE-2026-114938: Java4Shell Flaw Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Major Java Applications
content_md: A newly disclosed vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-114938 and dubbed Java4Shell exposes certain Java environments to memory corruption, sensitive data disclosure, service crashes, and potentially remote code execution. The flaw resides in OpenJDK’s hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder and can be triggered remotely when attacker-controlled Base64 data reaches the vulnerable Java runtime. Calif researchers demonstrated pre-authentication RCE against widely deployed enterprise applications running default configurations, including Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Authenticated exploitation was also demonstrated against Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker, while sample Spring Boot and Apache Struts applications were successfully exploited as well. The vulnerability is highly dependent on the underlying hardware. The vulnerable accelerated decoder runs on x86-64 processors supporting AVX-512 VBMI, including Intel Xeon Ice Lake and newer server platforms and AMD Zen 4 or later systems. ARM64 systems are not known to be affected by this specific flaw. Calif assigned Java4Shell a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2, Critical , while Oracle rates it 8.1, High under CVSS 3.1. Oracle released security updates on November 17, 2026, while several downstream Java vendors have been issuing their own patched builds on separate schedules.
